bibl.title: Long-Lasting Conceptual Change in Science Education

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: Collaborative argumentation among postgraduate students, and the argumentative dialogue inside it, as a route to durable conceptual change in science.
span.quote: In the present study, using a controlled experiment, we examined the value of collaborative argumentation for conceptual change in science education while fully considering the roles of argumentative dialogue.

span.label: existence
span.quote: The results revealed that collaborative argumentation had a delayed but long-lasting effect on conceptual change in science education (i.e., conceptual change induced by collaborative argumentation did not immediately indicate a significant improvement at the moments of argumentation but showed a significant improvement during the delay period).

span.label: conceptual change through collaborative argumentation
span.quote: The current study investigated the value of collaborative argumentation for conceptual change in science education.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: In the present study, using a controlled experiment, we examined the value of collaborative argumentation for conceptual change in science education while fully considering the roles of argumentative dialogue.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Misconceptions are robust, so an intervention that does start replacing them needs time before the replacement is measurable - which is why the benefit appears only at the delayed post-test.
span.quote: Thus, although a teaching approach or educational intervention could facilitate change from misconception to accurate understanding of scientific concepts, it may also require more time to explicitly show its effectiveness.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The three dialogue types complement one another - deliberation supplies critical reasoning, consensual co-construction repairs the social damage of disputes - so the productive profile is a mix, not one pure type.
span.quote: Thus, deliberative argumentation, disputative argumentation, and consensual co-construction might supplement each other to promote conceptual change in students.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Hearing group members voice both misconceptions and correct understandings makes a student self-reflect and spot the flaws in their own account, which is the route to conceptual change.
span.quote: collaborative argumentation provided opportunities for students to listen to others’ misconceptions and accurate understandings, prompting students to self-reflect and perceive the flaws in their own incomplete ideas

span.label: Hearing others' misconceptions makes a student's own incomplete idea visible to them, which is offered as the route from dialogue to conceptual change
span.quote: For example, collaborative argumentation provided opportunities for students to listen to others’ misconceptions and accurate understandings, prompting students to self-reflect and perceive the flaws in their own incomplete ideas.

span.label: Disagreement forces re-examination of evidence that was skipped the first time
span.quote: In addition, collaborative argumentation also provided opportunities for students to be trapped in a “tug-of-war” situation, prompting students to re-examine whether key evidence was neglected before.

span.label: Exposure to how others build a concept, not just what they conclude, is what changes the way of thinking rather than the answer
span.quote: For example, it provided opportunities for students to be exposed to others’ conceptualization processes of scientific concepts, prompting students to self-reflect and identify flaws in their ways of thinking.

span.label: Disputative dialogue works against learning by converting argument into a contest, which narrows openness to alternatives
span.quote: Perceptions of interpersonal competition might not only raise concerns about interpersonal relationships or senses of group belonging (Asterhan & Schwarz, 2016 ), but may also reduce cognitive flexibility and a person’s openness to alternative viewpoints (Carnevale & Probst, 1998 ).

span.label: Misconceptions are robust partly because teaching presents macro, sub-micro and symbolic representations side by side instead of teaching students to move between them
span.quote: In current science education, educators and teachers commonly present scientific concepts to students with the three levels of representations, rather than supporting students to develop multileveled ways of thinking (Johnstone, 2000 ; Taber, 2013 ).

span.label: Consensual co-construction alone consolidates a one-sided argument, which is why the productive pattern needs it together with deliberation rather than instead of it
span.quote: This dialogue between discussants showed mere development and consolidation of one-sided arguments, rather than challenging or juxtaposing different alternatives.

span.label: Small, almost entirely female sample
span.note: what this limits: the population every result speaks for: THE SAMPLE OF STUDENTS IN THIS STUDY WAS RELATIVELY SMALL, AND 95.65% OF STUDENTS WERE FEMALE
span.quote: First, the sample of students in this study was relatively small, and 95.65% of students were female.

span.label: Conducted online because of COVID-19, which may have changed the interpersonal tension of argumentation
span.note: what this limits: the argumentation findings specifically: THE CURRENT STUDY WAS CONDUCTED IN THE CONTEXT OF ONLINE LEARNING BECAUSE OF THE ... COVID-19 PANDEMIC, which may change the interpersonal character of argumentation
span.quote: Third, the current study was conducted in the context of online learning because of the significant disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

span.label: Cannot say whether the sequential ordering of dialogue types differed between high- and low-performing groups
span.note: what this limits: any claim about the ORDER of the dialogue types: IT WAS NOT ABLE TO REVEAL WHETHER THE SEQUENTIAL PATTERN OF ARGUMENTATIVE dialogue differed between high- and low-performing groups - the U-shape is a count, not a sequence
span.quote: Finally, although this study indicated that long-lasting conceptual change was associated with a U-shaped pattern of argumentative dialogue, it was not able to reveal whether the sequential pattern of argumentative dialogue differed in high-performing and low-performing groups.

span.label: Twenty-three students, almost all female, in one class at one university
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - 23 students, almost all female, one class at one university
span.quote: First, the sample of students in this study was relatively small, and 95.65% of students were female.

span.label: The authors' own confound for the headline result: students picked the topics themselves and had a month before the delayed post-test, so they may simply have gone and read more
span.note: what this limits: the headline conceptual-change result: THE TOPICS FOR THE THREE ARGUMENTATION ACTIVITIES WERE SELECTED BY MOST OF THE STUDENTS FROM A LIST OF TOPICS, so STUDENTS' TOPIC INTERESTS/PREFERENCES MAY BE ONE FACTOR THAT MAY DRIVE THEM TO SEARCH FOR MORE information
span.quote: Since the topics for the three argumentation activities were selected by most of the students from a list of topics, students’ topic interests/preferences may be one factor that may drive them to search for more information and resources about the topics and return better prepared for their delayed post-test 1 month later.

span.label: Conducted entirely online because of COVID-19, which the authors think may itself have softened the interaction and so shaped the dialogue types observed
span.note: what this limits: the argumentation behaviour that was measured: THE ONLINE ENVIRONMENT MAY HAVE RELIEVED THE TENSION THAT OFTEN EXISTS IN FACE-TO-FACE INTERPERSONAL INTERACTIONS, PROVIDING A MORE RELAXED ATMOSPHERE FOR STUDENTS TO ARGUE WITH GROUP MEMBERS
span.quote: The online environment may have relieved the tension that often exists in face-to-face interpersonal interactions, providing a more relaxed atmosphere for students to argue with group members using different types of argumentative dialogue.

span.label: The U-shaped pattern is a count of dialogue types, not their order, so nothing is known about sequence
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2 - the sequential pattern is not recoverable from these data
span.quote: Finally, although this study indicated that long-lasting conceptual change was associated with a U-shaped pattern of argumentative dialogue, it was not able to reveal whether the sequential pattern of argumentative dialogue differed in high-performing and low-performing groups.

span.label: The gender imbalance interacts directly with the finding, since the cited literature holds that women argue more deliberatively and men more disputatively - the very contrast the result rests on
span.note: what this limits: the dialogue-type outcome specifically, which is the paper's dependent variable: FEMALES ARE MORE INCLINED TO EXHIBIT DELIBERATIVE BEHAVIORS DURING SOCIAL INTERACTIONS, WHEREAS MALES ARE MORE INCLINED TO EXHIBIT DISPUTATIVE BEHAVIORS DURING SOCIAL INTERACTIONS
span.quote: Previous studies have suggested that females are more inclined to exhibit deliberative behaviors during social interactions, whereas males are more inclined to exhibit disputative behaviors during social interactions (Asterhan & Schwarz, 2016 ).

span.label: Group-level comparisons rest on two groups per activity in the first two studies, one high-performing and one low-performing
span.note: what this limits: every group-level comparison in the first two studies: they rest on two groups per activity, one high-performing and one low-performing
span.quote: Regarding the first argumentation activity, there were three groups in the collaborative argumentation condition. Group 5 was a low-performing group, and group 4 was a high-performing group, according to the mean substantive conceptual gains (i.e., gains from immediate post-test to delayed post-test) at the group level.

span.label: The tests are named as paired-sample t tests but compare two independent groups of different people, and the reported degrees of freedom (21) are those of an independent-samples test on 12 and 11 participants
span.note: what this limits: the inferential statistics, and this is an IDENTIFIED DEFECT rather than an author concession: COMPARISONS WERE CONDUCTED WITH PAIRED SAMPLE T TESTS while the groups compared are independent
span.quote: Comparisons were conducted with paired sample t tests. The results revealed students in the collaborative argumentation condition exhibited better conceptual understanding in the delayed phase of the two argumentation activities compared with students in the individual argumentation condition (see Fig. 7 ).

span.label: The reported N for the collaborative condition in the second activity is 11 in one sentence and 12 in another, within the same paragraph
span.note: what this limits: the reported sample size, also IDENTIFIED rather than declared: N = 12 here against N = 11 elsewhere for the same condition
span.quote: In addition, students in the collaborative argumentation condition also showed greater gains from pre-test to immediate post-test ( M = 30.00, SD = 15.90, N = 12) compared with students in the individual argumentation condition ( M = 13.75, SD = 17.34, N = 12), t (21) = 2.29, p < .05 (see Fig. 8b ).

span.label: a control group doing the SAME argumentation activity individually, against an experimental group doing it collaboratively
span.note: eliminates: that the conceptual change follows from doing the argumentation activity at all, rather than from doing it collaboratively · would have ruled out, had it been run: argumentation itself - and the time spent on it - as the explanation of conceptual change, which isolates the collaborative element as the only difference between the two groups
span.quote: Twenty-three postgraduate students were each allocated to one of two conditions (individual argumentation [control group] and collaborative argumentation [experimental group]) and participated in two argumentation activities.

span.label: symbolic
span.quote: The third term refers to symbolic representations, including formulae, equations, and mathematical manipulation and graphs, which act as a bridge between the aforementioned two levels by simultaneously representing both macro and sub-micro representations, as well as aiding students in shifting between these levels (Heng et al., 2015 ;Johnstone, 2000 ; Taber, 2013 ).

span.label: cognitive
span.quote: ( 2020 )’s multidimensional conceptual change framework, cognitive aspects of learning refer to change in conceptual contents.

span.label: long-lasting conceptual change → U-shaped pattern of argumentative dialogue
span.note: ASSOCIATION FOUND BY PROTOCOL ANALYSIS, direction not established: two high and one low - deliberative argumentation and co-consensual construction frequently occurred, while disputative argumentation rarely occurred.
span.quote: Dialogue protocol analysis revealed that long-lasting conceptual change was associated with a U-shaped pattern of argumentative dialogue (i.e., two high and one low: both deliberative argumentation and co-consensual construction frequently occurred, while disputative argumentation rarely occurred) in collaborative argumentation.

span.label: misconceptions → conceptual change
span.note: RESISTANCE, NOT PRODUCTION: many misconceptions are ROBUST AND RESISTANT to educational interventions and teaching approaches, which is what makes conceptual change difficult. No edge type can say a relation is an OBSTACLE, so the nearest available move asserted the opposite of what the sentence says.
span.quote: Science educators and practitioners have reported that it can be difficult to help students change their existing misconceptions to develop an accurate understanding of scientific concepts (i.e., conceptual change) because many misconceptions are robust and resistant to educational interventions and teaching approaches (Anderson & Smith, 1987 ; Asterhan & Dotan, 2018 ; Chi, 2005 ).

span.label: argumentative dialogue - deliberative: issue-driven rather than position-driven, with concessions made to sound arguments and no interpersonal tension
span.quote: (3) this dialogue was not position -driven but issue -driven. Even when there was disagreement between discussants, there were no manifest expressions of discomfort or interpersonal tension in the interaction.

span.label: argumentative dialogue - disputative: rich in critical reasoning but aimed at winning, treating argument as a win-lose contest
span.quote: The second type of argumentative dialogue refers to disputative dialogue, in which discussants defended a viewpoint and undermined alternative viewpoints to convince opponents to switch sides (Asterhan & Schwarz, 2016 ).

span.label: argumentative dialogue - consensual co-construction: agreeing and elaborating, which consolidates one side rather than juxtaposing alternatives
span.quote: The third type of argumentative dialogue is consensual co-construction, in which discussants transacted on each other’s contributions by agreeing with, elaborating on and expanding on ideas (Asterhan & Schwarz, 2016 ).

span.label: the effect at immediate post-test - absent: no significant difference between conditions right after the activity
span.quote: while there were not statistically significant differences in conceptual understanding in the pre-test and immediate post-test phases (see Fig. 7a )

span.label: the effect at delayed post-test - present: the difference appears a month later, which is the whole claim
span.quote: conceptual change induced by collaborative argumentation did not immediately indicate a significant improvement at the moments of argumentation but showed a significant improvement during the delay period

span.label: conceptual change - as a gain score between two phases, which is what 'substantive conceptual gains' means at group level
span.quote: Group 5 was a low-performing group, and group 4 was a high-performing group, according to the mean substantive conceptual gains (i.e., gains from immediate post-test to delayed post-test) at the group level.

span.label: conceptual change - as Chi's definition: restructuring misconceptions, explicitly NOT adding or gap-filling knowledge
span.quote: Chi ( 2008 ) argued that “conceptual change is not adding new knowledge or gap filling incomplete knowledge; rather, conceptual change is changing misconceptions in existing knowledge structures to an accurate understanding of scientific concepts”.

span.label: claim_type: existence

span.quote: The results revealed that collaborative argumentation had a delayed but long-lasting effect on conceptual change in science education

span.quote: Although collaborative argumentation is assumed to support such processes, its value for conceptual change is unclear.

span.label: builds-on → Asterhan and Schwarz (2016) three-type scheme of argumentative dialogue
span.quote: Finally, following a top-down scheme proposed by Asterhan and Schwarz ( 2016 ), initial coding efforts focused on three types of argumentative dialogue, considering whether the discussion could be characterized as deliberative argumentation, disputative argumentation, and co-consensual construction.

span.label: extends → Asterhan & Resnick (2020); McLure et al. (2020); Sampson & Clark (2009, 2011)
span.quote: Findings in this study not only echoes the previous studies but also further extends our understanding of the value of collaborative argumentation for conceptual change—the value of collaborative argumentation for conceptual change should be investigated and discussed under the broadened view of long-lasting science learning (Asterhan & Resnick, 2020 ; McLure et al., 2020 ; Sampson & Clark, 2009 , 2011 ).

span.label: extends → Asterhan and Schwarz (2016), the three-type scheme of argumentative dialogue
span.quote: Based on previous psychoeducational studies, Asterhan and Schwarz ( 2016 ) reviewed three types of argumentative dialogue in learning contexts: deliberative argumentation, disputative argumentation, and consensual co-construction.

span.quote: As suggested in Mclure et al. span.label: collaborative argumentation

span.label: stimulated recall interview

span.label: collaborative argumentation
span.quote: Collaborative argumentation refers to dialogical argumentation that takes place in groups of students when they are asked to work together on a common task of constructing an argument (Asterhan & Schwarz, 2007 ; Evagorou & Osborne, 2013 ).

span.label: consensual co-construction
span.quote: The third type of argumentative dialogue is consensual co-construction, in which discussants transacted on each other’s contributions by agreeing with, elaborating on and expanding on ideas (Asterhan & Schwarz, 2016 ).

span.label: U-shaped pattern
span.quote: a U-shaped pattern of argumentative dialogue (i.e., two high and one low: both deliberative argumentation and co-consensual construction frequently occurred, while disputative argumentation rarely occurred)

span.label: n = 23 — postgraduate science-education students who took part, mean age 24.83
span.quote: Twenty-three second-year postgraduate students (mean age = 24.83 years, SD = 1.90; one male, 22 female) at a large comprehensive university in central China participated in this study.

span.label: M = 75.92 ... M = 51.91 — delayed post-test conceptual understanding scores, collaborative vs. individual condition, activity 1
span.quote: Regarding the first argumentation activity, students in the collaborative argumentation condition exhibited significantly better conceptual understanding ( M = 75.92, SD = 10.65, N = 12) in the delayed post-test phase compared with students in the individual argumentation condition ( M = 51.91, SD = 22.81, N = 11, t [21] = 3.16, p < .001), while there were not statistically significant differences in conceptual understanding in the pre-test and immediate post-test phases

span.label: M = 24.67 ... M = 1.09 — gain from immediate to delayed post-test, collaborative vs. individual condition, activity 1
span.quote: Students in the collaborative argumentation condition showed significantly greater gains from immediate post-test to delayed post-test ( M = 24.67, SD = 13.51, N = 12) compared with students in the individual argumentation condition ( M = 1.09, SD = 22.81, N = 11), t (21) = 3.17, p < .001.

span.label: χ 2 [1, 2] = 14.962, p = .001 — dialogue-profile difference between high- and low-performing groups in the confirmatory third activity
span.quote: The results indicated that students in the high- and low-performing groups differed in argumentative dialogue ( χ 2 [1, 2] = 14.962, p = .001).
